title: Raising and reviewing a change request

steps.title: Change requests live under the Vault
steps.body: Which lives under Files. Open the Files tab.

steps.title: And its Change Requests view
steps.body: The Vault splits in two: the parts themselves, and the proposals to change them. Open Change Requests.

steps.title: Every proposed change, open and closed
steps.body: A change request is how a modification to a vaulted part gets agreed to before it becomes the current version.

steps.title: Title says what changes; rationale says why
steps.body: The rationale is the field that's still useful in six months, when nobody remembers the conversation that produced this.

steps.title: Constellation worked out what it affects
steps.body: The impact came from the BOM. You didn't have to remember which assemblies use this part — that's the whole reason the BOM is worth maintaining.

steps.title: Open the one you just raised
steps.body: Click the card. The review controls live inside it, not on the list.

steps.title: Normally someone else reviews this
steps.body: In your training project you're both people, so you'll review your own. That is an artefact of the sandbox, not how this works on real work. Approve and Reject only appear for officers — if you don't see them, skip ahead.

steps.title: Reject it, with a reason
steps.body: Rejecting isn't rude — "not until after the design review" is a real answer. If your account can't review change requests, skip this step; an officer will have shown you the same screen.

steps.title: It's still there, with the reason attached
steps.body: That record is what stops the same change being re-proposed blind in a month by someone who never heard the answer.
